Figure 3:Continuing geometric solving with new observations.
When new views are introduced, Solv3R continues solving from its existing state, jointly refining both previously reconstructed and newly added views.
DéjàView struggles to maintain consistent reconstruction.
Numbers indicate camera rotation errors in degrees.

Figure 4:Overview.Left: A stationary transformer block repeatedly updates the multi-view state through frame-wise and global attention, initial-state injection, and state normalization.
Right: The same operator continues refining the reconstruction across solver calls, allowing new views to be introduced at any stage and jointly updated with existing views.
Camera poses, depth maps, and ray maps can be decoded from the current state after any solver call.

Figure 8:Revising an existing reconstruction with new views.(a) Four views are solved for eight calls before twelve new views are introduced; camera colors indicate rotation error.
(b,c) Median rotation error of the original and new views during continued refinement over 96 windows.
Dashed curves in (b) indicate the no-join controls, where the original four views continue refinement for the same number of solver calls without introducing new views.
Solv3R incorporates new views while improving existing camera estimates, whereas DéjàView fails to maintain a consistent reconstruction.

Figure 10:Relocalization against a frozen map.Green dots are query estimates within 5 cm and 5∘of the ground truth (gray rings), and red crosses are the others, linked to their ground truth.
Above each panel are the cache size per map view and the fraction of queries within 5 cm and 5∘.
With the smallest cache, Solv3R localizes as many queries as the most accurate baseline.

Figure 11:Streaming reconstruction.Qualitative comparison with window-based reconstruction[26], recurrent-state methods[90,21], and geometric-context approaches[18]on long sequences, with camera trajectories colored by position error.

Figure 18:Failure case.In this window, views 5–8 share little content with views 1–4.
Solv3R places them at a wrong position and orientation within 16 calls and keeps them there up to call 64.

Figure 19:Reconstructions that grow as views arrive.Each row shows one scene at three stages of one arrival pattern.
Offline solves all views jointly, incremental adds the capture in thirds, streaming adds video frames one at a time, and arbitrary order adds random groups of views.
Views that join continue the running solve, and the views already in it keep their states.
Above each panel are the number of views in the solve and the numberKKof solver calls run so far.
Arrows give the views that joined, and orange marks their cameras.

Figure 20:One scene under the four arrival patterns.Shown as inFig.19.
All four patterns end in nearly the same reconstruction, although the views arrive in different orders and receive different numbers of calls.

Figure 21:Offline reconstruction comparison.All methods see the same 100 images at once.
VGGT, DA3-L, and VGGT-Ω\Omegamisplace the second room, while Solv3R reconstructs both rooms in one piece.
Figure 22:Offline reconstruction comparison.All methods see the same 44 images at once.π3\pi^{3}and DA3-L misplace parts of the scene, while Solv3R keeps the walls and floor in place.

Figure 23:Offline reconstruction comparison.All methods see the same 100 images at once, and the ceiling is removed for display.
Insets show the predicted cameras in color and the reference cameras in gray, seen from above.
Solv3R places the cameras closest to the reference, while VGGT and VGGT-Ω\Omegafold the room.

Figure 24:Streaming reconstruction comparison.The methods and settings are those of the streaming figure of the main paper.
Camera trajectories are colored by position error.
